paragraphs: Language can influence how people think about other groups. It can help make violence appear necessary, justified, or unavoidable, and can therefore be used as a tool to move people toward acts of violence.

A particularly serious form of such linguistic mobilization is direct and public incitement to genocide. This is punishable under the 1948 UN Genocide Convention. On January 26, 2024, the International Court of Justice ordered Israel to take measures to prevent genocide against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip. This includes preventing and punishing public and direct incitement to genocide.

This visualization shows recurring linguistic patterns that can legitimize violence or mobilize people for violence. It does not provide a legal classification of the statements, but aims to improve awareness of how language is used.

The statements analyzed come from the [Intent](https://intent.law4palestine.org/) dataset by the Palestinian NGO Law for Palestine. The patterns were developed from the statements through qualitative content analysis.

statementNotes.title: Enemy-image frame
statementNotes.body: The statement mobilizes support for extreme violence by framing destruction as necessary for collective survival.

statementNotes.title: No-alternative frame
statementNotes.body: The statement presents "crushing Hamas and razing Gaza" as the only condition for collective survival.
